## Source code

The complete pipeline – mesh extraction, descriptor computation, surface registration, statistical shape modelling, association analyses, and figure generation – is open source:

<https://github.com/AnatolAicher/NAKO-Ribcage-SSM>

The repository README documents the environment, the preset-driven pipeline driver (`scripts/run_pipeline.py`), and the run-directory layout; the Scalismo registration stage lives under `environment/scalismo_ssm/`.

## Canonical run

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(run_info_md(r))
```

Runs are configured by a YAML preset. The template for the full-cohort analysis is [`presets/full_analysis.example.yaml`](https://github.com/AnatolAicher/NAKO-Ribcage-SSM/blob/main/presets/full_analysis.example.yaml); [`presets/example.yaml`](https://github.com/AnatolAicher/NAKO-Ribcage-SSM/blob/main/presets/example.yaml) documents every key.

## Shape-model release

The mean shape, the principal-component modes, and the demographics-to-shape generator ([Methods §2.8.6](manuscript.qmd#sec-geometry-generator)) are released as a 6 MB bundle with a NumPy-only loader in the [`model/`](https://github.com/AnatolAicher/NAKO-Ribcage-SSM/tree/main/model) directory of the code repository and archived on Zenodo under DOI [10.5281/zenodo.22230693](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22230693). The [SSM Viewer](viewer.qmd) embeds the same model.

## Participant-level data

Due to data privacy regulations in the context of the NAKO cohort, the individual-level metadata and imaging data used in this project cannot be released publicly. NAKO data can be obtained via the electronic application portal at <https://www.nako.de/transferhub>. Specific derived data may be available on request from the corresponding author (<anatol.aicher@uzh.ch>), subject to NAKO data access policies.
